ordered_sample.primary_outcome: Disease-specific disability, Roland Morris Disability Questionnaire (first-named of two co-primary measures; the other is lumbar pain, LBP Rating Scale)
ordered_sample.primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary outcome measures were disease-specific disability Roland Morris Questionnaire (RMDQ) and lumbar pain (LBP Rating Scale).
ordered_sample.anchor_as_printed: At baseline, 100 days follow-up, 1-year follow-up the disease-specific disability-RMDQ changed: antibiotic 15, 11, 5.7; placebo 15, 14, 14

ordered_sample.primary_outcome: Composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, or nonfatal stroke (time to first event)
ordered_sample.primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary composite outcome was the first occurrence of death from cardiovascular causes, nonfatal myocardial infarction (including silent), or nonfatal stroke.
ordered_sample.anchor_as_printed: The primary outcome occurred in 108 of 1648 patients (6.6%) in the semaglutide group and in 146 of 1649 patients (8.9%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.58 to 0.95; P<0.001 for noninferiority)

ordered_sample.primary_outcome: Ability to work at 4-month follow-up (first-named outcome in the abstract; no primary outcome is designated)

ordered_sample.primary_outcome: Composite of 40% decline in eGFR, kidney failure (dialysis or transplant), or death due to kidney disease
ordered_sample.primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary end point was the composite of the first occurrence of a sustained 40% decrease in eGFR, the development of kidney failure (defined as a need for maintenance dialysis or kidney transplant), or death due to kidney disease.
ordered_sample.anchor_as_printed: Over a mean of 4.2 years of follow-up, the primary outcome occurred in 74 participants (28.8%) in the methylprednisolone group compared with 106 (43.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio [HR], 0.53 [95% CI, 0.39-0.72]; P < .001; absolute annual event rate difference, -4.8% per year [95% CI, -8.0% to -1.6%])
ordered_sample.notes: full-dose and reduced-dose regimens pooled vs placebo; JAMA PDF via Zaid JAMA login

ordered_sample.primary_outcome: State and trait anxiety (Spielberger STAI) during an IVF-ET procedure with vs without dietary sodium restriction (no primary is designated)
ordered_sample.primary_outcome_source: Abstract: influences of dietary sodium restriction as an independent factor on anxiety levels of women participating in an in vitro fertilization-embryo transfer procedure were investigated.
ordered_sample.anchor_as_printed: State as well as trait anxiety scores increased significantly (p = 0.01, and p = 0.03, respectively) from baseline to the point of measurement in the luteal phase. No significant differences in this mean increase were observed between the two diet groups
ordered_sample.notes: 1999, 119 randomized, 69 analysed; no registration; abstract text layer is OCR of a scan, quote cleaned; T&F PDF saved by Zaid

ordered_sample.primary_outcome: Lowest SpO2 during the first intubation attempt
ordered_sample.primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary endpoint was lowest SpO2 during the first intubation attempt.
ordered_sample.anchor_as_printed: Median lowest SpO2 during the first intubation attempt was 100% in both groups. Incidence of SpO2 falling below 90% was lower in the intervention group (15.5%) compared to the control group (22.6%) (adjusted relative risk=0.68, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.37–1.25)

ordered_sample.primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary end point was locally assessed progression-free survival, according to RECIST, version 1.1.
ordered_sample.anchor_as_printed: The duration of progression-free survival was significantly longer in the ribociclib group than in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.43 to 0.72; P=3.29×10−6 for superiority)

ordered_sample.primary_outcome: Full clinical remission at the end of the 3-year trial phase (first of two hierarchical primary end points; second is decrease in eGFR of ≥15 ml/min/1.73 m2)
ordered_sample.primary_outcome_source: Methods: The two primary end points in hierarchical order were full clinical remission (protein-to-creatinine ratio <0.2 and decrease in eGFR <5 ml/min/1.73 m2 from baseline) and a decrease in eGFR of at least 15 ml/min/1.73 m2 at the end of the 3-year trial phase.
ordered_sample.anchor_as_printed: After 3 years, 4 patients (5%) in the supportive-care group, as compared with 14 (17%) in the immunosuppression group, had a full clinical remission (P = 0.01)
ordered_sample.notes: hierarchical co-primary; second end point: 22 (28%) vs 21 (26%), P = 0.75

ordered_sample.primary_outcome: Change from baseline in 24-hour urine protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months, felzartamab vs placebo
ordered_sample.primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary endpoint was the change from baseline in 24-hour urine protein:creatinine ratio (UPCR) at 9 months.
ordered_sample.anchor_as_printed: Treatment with felzartamab versus placebo led to rapid (within 3-6 months) reduction in least-squares mean UPCR sustained at nine months (placebo, -5.7%; 2-dose, -12.5%; 5-dose, -12.8%; 9-dose, -29.5%; part 2, -44.8%)
ordered_sample.notes: REPLACEMENT for align; phase 2a with several dose arms and a part 2; abstract gives arm percentages, no CI; Kidney Int open access, fetched in Chrome

ordered_sample.primary_outcome: Change in HbA1c from baseline to 26 weeks (modified intention-to-treat), LY3298176 doses vs placebo and vs dulaglutide
ordered_sample.primary_outcome_source: Methods: The primary efficacy outcome was change in HbA1c from baseline to 26 weeks in the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population.
ordered_sample.anchor_as_printed: Mean changes from baseline in HbA1c with LY3298176 were -1.06% for 1 mg, -1.73% for 5 mg, -1.89% for 10 mg, and -1.94% for 15 mg, compared with -0.06% for placebo
